column3:
The heart of the product. One component, N states driven by the framework payload. The
largest single ticket in the project; it is deliberately not split across two people because
it is one file and the merge cost would exceed the parallelism.

Acceptance criteria
* Competency name and tappable level descriptors, both read from the framework payload. No
  competency name, scale bound or descriptor appears in code.
* Narrative with debounced autosave via PATCH /entries/{id}, with a visible saved / saving /
  failed indicator.
* Evidence row: attach via POST /entries/{id}/evidence, remove via DELETE /evidence/{id},
  respecting the type and size limits the framework sets.
* Self-score via PUT /entries/{id}/scores/self. PUT because it is an upsert: a student may
  change their mind before submitting. That is deliberate, not an inconsistency to tidy.
* "Competency 3 of 6" progress, Back and Next, Submit on the last one.
* Submit failures map back to the offending entries. NARRATIVE_REQUIRED, SELF_SCORE_MISSING
  and EVIDENCE_REQUIRED each return entry ids in details; walk the user to the first one
  rather than showing a generic banner.
* draft is the only editable state. A submitted reflection renders read-only.
* All four states.

Depends on CAP-3, CAP-4, CAP-5. Blocks CAP-12, CAP-13, CAP-20.

Acceptance criteria
* Confirms the assessor has been notified. Notifications are derived from events, not stored;
  there is no notifications table and this ticket does not add one.
* Shows the next sprint's date if there is one.
* Back to diary.
* All four states.

Depends on CAP-11.

The same component as CAP-11 in a second mode, not a second component. Sequence this after
CAP-11 merges rather than running them in parallel.

Acceptance criteria
* Student narrative and evidence read-only. Their self-score visible.
* Level picker posting to POST /entries/{id}/scores. POST rather than PUT because a second
  attempt is an error, not an update.
* Comment box becomes required when the counter-score is below the self-score, and whenever
  the framework's comment_required flag is set. The disabled button is a convenience; the
  400 COMMENT_REQUIRED is the rule and the UI must handle it arriving anyway.
* A 409 on a repeat counter-score is surfaced clearly, not swallowed. Re-scoring is out of
  scope by decision (ADR #34). Do not build a way around it.
* The reflection flips to assessed on its own once every entry has a counter-score. The UI
  reflects that; it does not trigger it.
* All four states.

Depends on CAP-10, CAP-11.

column2: CAP-14 · History sheet: the event timeline
column3:
First candidate for de-scope if Sprint 4 runs hot.

Acceptance criteria
* GET /reflections/{id}/events rendered as a timeline inside a BottomSheet.
* One row per event type, readable by a person, with the actor and the timestamp converted
  from stored UTC to local.
* All four states. Empty is reachable on a fresh draft.

Depends on CAP-4, CAP-5.

Acceptance criteria
* Available templates and saved copies listed separately.
* The Edit action is hidden when in_use. A framework referenced by any reflection is
  permanently read-only, because mutating it would silently change what past students were
  scored against.
* Assign posts to POST /framework-assignments.
* A gig takes exactly one rubric. A second assignment is refused by FrameworkAssigner and by
  ak_fw_assignments at the database (ADR #35). Surface the 409. Do not build a replace flow:
  there is no endpoint, and the answer to "I picked the wrong rubric" is a new gig (ADR #33).
* All four states.

Depends on CAP-3, CAP-5. Blocks CAP-16.

Copy-then-edit. The scope here is narrower than it looks and the temptation is to widen it.

Acceptance criteria
* Based-on selector, name field, competencies with their level descriptors.
* Save creates a copy via POST /frameworks (deep copy), then PATCH /frameworks/{id},
  PATCH /competencies/{id} and PATCH /levels/{id}.
* Renaming competencies and rewording descriptors ONLY. No creating a framework from scratch,
  no adding or removing competencies, no changing level counts (ADR #16). Do not add UI for
  any of them, not even disabled.
* 409 FRAMEWORK_IN_USE surfaced plainly if the guard fires mid-edit.
* All four states.

Depends on CAP-15.

column2: CAP-17 · PDF export: the dompdf decision, the ADR and the implementation
column3:
The one remaining backend gap. It was left open deliberately as a package decision for the
team, so the decision is part of this ticket, not a prerequisite to it.

Acceptance criteria
* An ADR in docs/adr/ recording the choice of dompdf and what was rejected. Appended, never
  rewritten.
* POST /exports accepts pdf and the queued job renders it. The exports row is the job record
  (ADR #30); status is stored, not derived (ADR #25).
* The PDF carries the reflections, both score sets, the framework version snapshot and the
  radar. This is the student-owned record leaving the system, so it has to stand alone
  without the application to interpret it.
* docs/openapi.yaml updated in the same PR, not afterwards.
* Download authorisation holds: another student's export is a 404, not a 403.
* Feature tests for render, authorisation and the failure path.

No dependencies. Start day one of the sprint.

Acceptance criteria
* PDF and JSON selector, plus a summary of what the export includes.
* Request, receive 202 with a job id, poll GET /exports/{id}, download.
* Polling backs off and eventually gives up with a readable error rather than spinning
  forever.
* Five states here, not four: the in-progress state is its own thing and is not the loading
  skeleton.

Depends on CAP-4, CAP-17.

column2: CAP-19 · Policies covering every remaining permission-matrix row
column3:
Marked [~] in the scope document. GigPolicy, ReflectionPolicy, FrameworkPolicy and
ExportPolicy exist; the rows they do not cover belong to resources that did not exist when
they were written. Those resources exist now.

Acceptance criteria
* Every row of the permission matrix in docs/api-reference.html has a policy method behind it.
* Roles resolve server-side through RoleResolver from gig_participants, for the gig in
  question. The client never sends a role.
* Authorisation lives in api/app/Policies/ and nowhere else. Not in a controller, not in a
  FormRequest, not duplicated into the frontend.
* Not-yours returns 404 rather than 403, deliberately indistinguishable from does-not-exist.
* A feature test per row, including the negative case. The negative case is the point.

No dependencies.

column2: CAP-20 · Prove the framework swap: SFIA 9 end to end, no code change
column3:
Definition of done item 5, and the claim the entire product rests on. If this needs a code
change, the rubric is not really data and that is the most important bug in the project.

Acceptance criteria
* A new gig assigned SFIA 9 rather than the La Trobe rubric. A new gig, not an edited seed.
* The stepper renders SFIA's competencies and descriptors, and the radar renders SFIA's axes.
* The scale comes from v_framework_scale, where each skill is valid over only part of the
  seven levels, so the ranges are uneven per competency and the radar has to cope.
* Zero frontend and zero backend code changes required. Any that are needed are logged as
  bugs and fixed inside this ticket.
* Written up as a short verification note and screenshotted for the client demo.

Depends on CAP-6, CAP-11, CAP-15.
